one_liner: C++20 SIMD wrapper (eve::wide) with a large vectorised math library and SIMD STL-style algorithms; successor of Boost.SIMD, no published speedups.
what_it_does: EVE gives you a value type eve::wide<T, N> that maps onto SSE2 to AVX-512, NEON/ASIMD or fixed-size SVE registers, plus element-wise function objects that accept both scalars and wides: core, math (about 70 benchmarked functions such as cos, sincos, exp, log, pow, atan2, tanpi), special, bessel, elliptic, polynomial, combinatorial and complex. A separate eve::algo layer offers range algorithms (find, mismatch, transform, reduce, transform_reduce, copy_if, keep_if, inclusive_scan, set_intersection, min_element and others) with views and SoA containers. It is a different interface, not a drop-in for scalar loops or std::experimental::simd, although it tries to follow standard naming. The instruction set is fixed at compile time; runtime dispatch means building one shared library per ISA (eve_build_variants) and picking it with eve::is_supported plus dlopen, as in examples/multi-arch.
how_it_is_fast: Explicit SIMD: each function is implemented per instruction-set family with intrinsics behind tag dispatch, so the code you write once compiles to the widest registers the target flags allow instead of relying on auto-vectorisation. Math functions are vectorised polynomial approximations whose range reduction can be narrowed with decorators (cos[quarter_circle], cos[half_circle], cos[medium], cos[big], exp[raw], [fast]) so callers who know their input range skip the expensive reduction. The algorithm layer handles alignment, tails and unrolling through traits (no_aligning, expensive-kernel and fused-operation traits added in 2023.02.15).
when_to_use: Portable C++20 code that must vectorise the same source for x86 (SSE2 to AVX-512) and ARM (NEON A32/A64, ASIMD, SVE at fixed 128/256/512 bits)
Bulk float/double transcendental work (sin/cos/exp/log/pow and the d/pi variants) where you can state the input range and use the reduced-range decorators
Byte and integer scans or filters (find, mismatch, copy_if, keep_if, set_intersection) over contiguous ranges that you want written once instead of per-ISA intrinsics
Projects already on GCC 13+, Clang 16+ or MSVC 19.44+ that can ship one binary per ISA or compile with -march for a known fleet
when_not_to_use: You need evidence before adopting: the repo publishes no benchmark results and no comparison against Highway, xsimd, std::simd or vector libm; measure your kernel yourself

Pre-C++20 toolchains, or codebases that need a stable API: the README calls EVE a research project whose API and minimum compiler may change before a 0.1 release, and the last tag is v2023.02.15 while main has moved on
Scalable (length-agnostic) SVE, RISC-V V or GPUs: SVE is fixed-size only, PowerPC VMX/VSX is partial, GPGPU is out of scope
Single-binary runtime dispatch across ISAs without dlopen: EVE has no built-in function multiversioning, only the per-variant shared-library pattern
Debug (-O0) builds on hot paths: issue #1740 reports eve::algo::copy about 40x slower than std::ranges::copy at -O0, and the maintainers advise memcpy/memmove for plain byte copies

integration.dependencies: none external; kumi, raberu and spy are vendored under include/eve/deps
integration.min_toolchain: C++20; g++ 13+, clang++ 16+, MSVC 19.44+ (recommended g++ 14+, clang++ 19+)
integration.platforms: x86 SSE2 to AVX2/FMA3 and AVX-512 (Skylake-AVX512 subset), ARM NEON A32/A64, ASIMD, SVE fixed 128/256/512; PowerPC VMX/VSX partial; no dynamic-length SVE

gotchas: Build with -DNDEBUG: without it asserts stay in the generated code; open issue #2085 (Ryzen 9 7940HS, g++ 14.2.1 and clang++ 19.1.7) measured a 4-lane float gather at 0.198 ns with -O3 and 1.01 ns with -O3 -mavx2, about 5x slower, still unresolved; EVE_USE_BMI_ON_AVX2 is documented as 'beneficial on Intel, disastrous on AMD'.

Harness flaw in the repo's own benchmarks (no published numbers depend on it): 24 math 'regular' benchmarks (sin, cos, tan, sincos, sec, csc, cot, their d/pi variants, atan2, atan2d, atan2pi) draw inputs with std::uniform_real_distribution<double>(valmin, valmax); for double this violates the b - a <= max precondition and libstdc++ returns +inf for every element (reproduced locally with g++: 11,776 of 11,776 inputs were inf), so the std::cos versus eve::cos double rows time only the inf-to-NaN path; the float rows are valid but every input has |x| >= 1e30, so they time only huge-argument reduction.

Other benchmark build defects: the MSVC bench flags read /0x (zero) instead of /Ox, and the GCC/Clang bench flags are -O3 without -march, so a default configure benchmarks SSE2 unless you add CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS; benchmarks are OFF by default (EVE_BUILD_BENCHMARKS) and compare only against scalar std:: functions.
README's licence block prints MIT text under a 'Boost Software License' heading; LICENSE.md is BSL-1.0, which the project adopted in 2022.09.0 when it moved from MIT.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick EVE over Vector Class Library (also numberless in this catalogue) when you need ARM NEON or fixed-size SVE builds or STL-style SIMD algorithms on top of the wrapper; pick math_intrinsics or SIMD-math-prims when you only need a few approximate float functions in plain C with published libm comparisons. vstat, a catalogued sibling, is built on EVE and is the closest thing to third-party performance evidence for it.
verified_claims_summary: Nothing measured: the README states a goal ('efficient, low-level, high-abstraction') and cites PACT 2012, HPCS 2018 and an older Scalable Computing paper without results, and the benchmarks/ nanobench harness (std:: scalar function versus eve scalar and eve::wide of 64 bytes, 92 KiB arrays, warmup 1500) has no committed output. The 2023 LMU bachelor thesis that compared six C++ SIMD libraries against intrinsics was unreachable, so whether EVE was among them is still unknown.
status_note: Actively developed (2,059 commits, latest 2026-10-11, 1.4k stars) and BSL-1.0, header-only and copyable, but still a self-described research project with no tagged release since v2023.02.15 and 102 open issues.
